primary_topics: Chapter 5 of 'Judicial Renaissance' -- CJP's remarks opening the ninth Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. Distinguished Lecture Series session, in which he frames the whole set of Davide retirement activities as a single 'Celebration of Thanksgiving.'

A running account of the Lecture Series itself: its Filipino lecturers, its foreign legal luminaries, the Kennedy lecture cancelled by Chief Justice Rehnquist's death, and today's nine-speaker panel on 'The Commitment to Judicial Education.'

A numbered inventory of the fourteen valedictory projects lined up by the Valedictory Executive Committee, from speeches, documentary and coffee-table book through awards, essays and PERLAS to the ASEAN Law Association Conference and the International Conference and Showcase on Judicial Reforms.

A public naming of the Valedictory Executive Committee's members, project assignments and support staff, and a closing argument that the APJR will outlast Davide's own term because the reforms are institutional rather than personal.
sub_topics: The Lecture Series, begun February 9, 2005, is described as a monthly academic pursuit drawing attention to the aspirations and achievements of the Court during the Chief's seven-year term.

Past lectures are recalled in order: Jose C. Vitug on the legal profession in the digital age, Reynato S. Puno on legislative investigations and privacy, Raul C. Pangalangan on Davide's judicial philosophy, and Fr. Joaquin G. Bernas on Davide's constitutional drafting.
Jovito R. Salonga -- CJP's 'esteemed guru,' called by Senator Joker Arroyo the 'Last Titan of the 20th Century' -- spoke on July 28, 2005 on maintaining public faith and confidence in the judiciary.

Three international lecturers are named: Justice Michael Donald Kirby of the High Court of Australia, President Rodolfo de Leon Molina of the Supreme Court of Guatemala, and the World Bank's Anthony Gerald Toft.

Justice Anthony Kennedy's scheduled September 12, 2005 lecture was cancelled when the death of US Chief Justice William Rehnquist required him to attend the wake; rescheduling was still being discussed.

Today's session, 'The Commitment to Judicial Education,' is unique in bringing nine personalities under one roof for a retrospect of Philippine judicial education and a discussion of court-annexed mediation, capped by Philja Chancellor Ameurfina A. Melencio Herrera on the future.

The session is the first of three lectures on the APJR, to be followed by CJP's own 'Overall Perspective of the Philippine Judicial Reform Program' on October 19, 2005 and by the Chief Justice's valedictory lecture on December 13, 2005.
The Lecture Series is placed in context as only one of many activities collectively called the 'Celebration of Thanksgiving.'

Projects 1-4: print and digital issuance of Davide's speeches, decisions and dissents; a TV documentary; a coffee-table book and photo essay; and a concert plus a Philippine dance and musical festival by SC officials and employees.

Projects 5-7: the publication of CJP's own book 'Judicial Renaissance'; a traveling exhibit on Davide's life and thoughts in Manila, Cagayan de Oro, Pampanga and Cebu; and Open Houses of Halls of Justice to teach the public, especially youth, about access to justice.

Projects 8-12: a nationwide law-student essay contest on 'Judicial Reforms Under the Davide Watch'; Judicial Excellence Awards; the Chief Justice Davide Awards for model judiciary employees; the Davide Reform Awards for APJR contributors; and PERLAS, a rule-of-law education project for elementary and high school students.

Projects 13-14: co-sponsorship of the ASEAN Law Association Conference of November 24-26, 2005 and the International Conference and Showcase on Judicial Reforms of November 28-30, 2005, called by far the most important commemorative project.
The ICSJR is described as combining plenary addresses and workshops with an exhibit in which judicial modernization projects can be seen, touched and in some cases operated by participants.

CJP stresses that the valedictory activities are intellectual, cultural, social and sporting, and involve every constituency of the Judicial Branch from justices to law students and the general public.
As committee chair he publicly recognizes for the first time the SC magistrates on the Committee and each member's specific project assignment, then the entire support staff by name.
He closes by noting that when Davide gave his 1998 vision-mission statement no one expected the APJR to draw the total support of foreign judiciaries and agencies such as the UN, World Bank and ADB.

The APJR's far-reaching vision is restated: a corps of competent, dedicated, honest and courageous judges, speedier high-quality justice, and a judicial system trusted even when its rulings are unpalatable.

Davide's personal stewardship ends by operation of law at the mandatory retirement age of 70 on December 20, 2005, but the Committee is sure the reform projects will continue as cornerstones of the judicial renaissance he stewarded.

stances.claim: The tribute owed a retiring Chief Justice is not ceremony for its own sake but a 'Celebration of Thanksgiving' whose every activity is centered on the APJR -- the reform program Davide himself called the centerpiece of his stewardship.
stances.rhetorical_move: reframing commemoration as program advocacy: fourteen numbered activities are shown to converge on a single reform agenda rather than on the man

stances.claim: The APJR's reach exceeded anyone's expectation in 1998, drawing not only Philippine officialdom and public support but the backing of foreign judiciaries and agencies such as the United Nations, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.
stances.rhetorical_move: expectation-versus-outcome contrast, with named international institutions supplied as the proof of reach

stances.claim: Davide's personal stewardship ends by operation of law at 70, but the reforms he envisioned will continue after him and will stand as the cornerstones of the judicial renaissance he stewarded.
stances.rhetorical_move: institution-outlasts-the-person argument used as the valedictory peroration, converting a retirement into a continuity pledge

stances.claim: The ultimate goal of reform is a judicial system that enjoys the full trust and confidence of the people because its actions and decisions are judicious and prudent, even though they may sometimes be unpalatable to current public sentiment.
stances.rhetorical_move: trust-not-popularity distinction: public confidence is defined by the quality of judgments rather than by their popular reception

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 5 of 'Judicial Renaissance' collects the remarks Justice Panganiban delivered at the ninth session of the Chief Justice Hilario G. Davide Jr. Distinguished Lecture Series, a monthly series begun on February 9, 2005 to mark the aspirations and achievements of the Court during Davide's seven-year term. He recapped the lectures already given -- Jose C. Vitug on the legal profession in the digital age, Reynato S. Puno on legislative investigations and privacy, Raul C. Pangalangan on Davide's judicial philosophy, Fr. Joaquin G. Bernas on his role in drafting the 1987 Constitution, and Jovito R. Salonga, whom he called his esteemed guru and whom Senator Joker Arroyo had called the 'Last Titan of the 20th Century,' on maintaining public faith in the judiciary -- along with three international lecturers, Australia's Michael Donald Kirby, Guatemala's Rodolfo de Leon Molina and the World Bank's Anthony Gerald Toft, and noted that Justice Anthony Kennedy's scheduled September 12 lecture had been cancelled by the death of Chief Justice Rehnquist. He then introduced the day's nine-speaker panel on 'The Commitment to Judicial Education,' the first of three lectures on what Davide called the centerpiece of his stewardship, the Action Program for Judicial Reforms. The bulk of the address was a numbered inventory of fourteen valedictory activities collectively styled a 'Celebration of Thanksgiving': publication of Davide's speeches and opinions, a TV documentary, a coffee-table book, a concert and dance festival, CJP's own book 'Judicial Renaissance,' a traveling exhibit, Open Houses of Halls of Justice, a law-student essay contest, three sets of awards, the PERLAS rule-of-law education project, the ASEAN Law Association Conference and the International Conference and Showcase on Judicial Reforms of November 28-30, 2005. He publicly named the Valedictory Executive Committee's members, their assignments and its support staff, praising their unpaid labor, and closed by insisting that although Davide's stewardship ended at the mandatory retirement age of 70 on December 20, 2005, the reforms would endure as the cornerstones of the judicial renaissance he had stewarded.
